subject: Population level confidence intervals without parboot

messages.author: e28e0b4fcf6aa261
messages.subject: Population level confidence intervals without parboot
parts:
Hello all,


I’m using gdistsamp to estimate abundance. I've used predict to get abundance estimates for a large number of fine scale pixels. I've taken the estimate of the total population size to be the sum of the predicted value for all pixels and I'm now trying to calculate a confidence interval for this value. I've tried to use parboot for this but due to the large number of pixels it’s going to take weeks to run. 


Is there a way I can calculate a confidence interval manually or will I need to increase my pixel size (i.e. reduce the number of pixels) until parboot will run in a reasonable timeframe?


We’re concerned that simply adding up the lower and upper predicted values for all pixels might unduly inflate the CIs because it assumes positive covariance among pixels. We’d like to use something like the delta method, assuming there is no covariance among pixels.


I’ve tried taking the square root of the sum of the squared SEs for all pixels, multiplying by 1.96 and adding to/subtracting from the total population estimate to get a 95% CI. I did this on the log scale since that’s what the model uses for abundance, but I end up with “Inf” when I try to back transform the resulting values so clearly that’s not quite right.


Any advice would be much appreciated.


Many thanks,


Zoe

messages.author: 4a635fe980c8c1cd
messages.subject: Re: Population level confidence intervals without parboot
parts:
Hi Zoe,

You could use the delta method. Just to re-use some dummy code posted elsewhere, to get an estimate of Var(N-hat), you could try something like:

library(emdbook)
Var_hat<-deltavar(sum(exp(b0+b1*Forest)), 
                         meanval=c(b0=estimateb0, b1=estimateb1),
                          Sigma=[variance and covariance for b0, b1])
SE<-sqrt(Var_hat)

Above, assume 'Forest' is a pixel level covariate, so a vector of length nPixels--you'd have to change the beta arguments, lengths, etc. as needed. The variance covariance matrix can be grabbed from the fitted model. 

There are a couple of options for constructing the CI. Maybe a lognormal approach makes the most sense. Something like dropping the exp in the deltavar call, and exponentiating log[LCI, UCI]--should be able find some formal descriptions around.

I guess you could also use monte carlo simulation based on the predicted pixel values and estimated variance, although I don't know that there would be any substantive advantage to doing so.  

The approaches above focus on expected abundance (a lambda_i rather than the latent N_i), but if you've only sampled a small number of the cells you are trying to predict across, the difference in the CI shouldn't be substantial.

John
